close_reason:
Resolved by JMAP-qz9v.29 (closed). The bead's option (c) ('document the placeholder dance in the trait doc') was applied as part of qz9v.29's 'sentinel fields the backend MUST replace' contract addition. ContactsBackend::create_object's rustdoc at backend.rs:82-114 now documents the id-placeholder pattern explicitly:

> Sentinel fields the backend MUST replace
> - id: The id field in the input object is always set to 'placeholder' so the typed Deserialize on O (AddressBook / ContactCard) succeeds. The backend MUST replace it with a real, unique, account-scoped id...

Bead options (a) 'make Id optional on deserialize' and (b) 'pass raw Value into create_object' are workspace-design questions filed separately if revisited; option (c) was the recommended low-cost path and is done.
description:
What is awkward: addressbook.rs:124-126 and card.rs:105-107 inject 'id': 'placeholder' into the create object before calling serde_json::from_value::<AddressBook | ContactCard>. The reason given in inline comments is that the type requires 'id' to deserialize. Then MemoryBackend.create_object (memory.rs:612, 617-620) mints a real id, serializes the obj, and overwrites the 'id' field on the resulting Value.

So the placeholder is created, deserialized into a typed object, the typed object is serialized BACK out, the placeholder is overwritten with the real id, and finally the typed object is deserialized again from the post-substitution Value. Three serde round-trips with the id sometimes being a placeholder string and sometimes the real one.

Suggested rewrite paths (any one):
 (a) Make ContactCard / AddressBook deserialize with a missing or default-id (Id::empty(), or Option<Id> on the wire). The default-Id approach is what jmap-types should provide.
 (b) Have the handler pass the raw Value into create_object and let the backend handle id assignment without the typed round-trip on the handler side. The current shape forces the placeholder dance because the backend trait takes O: SetObject.
 (c) Accept the placeholder dance as the canonical pattern and document it in the trait doc — 'create_object receives a partially-constructed object whose id is a placeholder; mint a real id and return (real_id, updated_obj)'.

Today the placeholder dance happens in addressbook.rs, card.rs, and the canonical mail-server's email.rs (likely also mailbox.rs). If it's the canonical pattern, it deserves a one-line note on ContactsBackend::create_object explaining 'the obj parameter has a placeholder id; mint a real one'. Otherwise it's a confusing serialize-deserialize-serialize-deserialize loop for new readers.
title: MemoryBackend.create_object inserts placeholder id from caller, then immediately overwrites — drop the placeholder injection or document why
